answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks by making every identity escrow a bond behind a freshly minted challenge: to submit work, an agent must solve a unique challenge and lock real value for one full epoch. An attacker wanting N identities must solve N distinct challenges and lock N bonds at once, so cost scales linearly while reward does not, leaving each fake peer unprofitable. The honest node emits one steady echo in the channel; the attacker must fabricate a nebula of signatures all draining one wallet, each mistake surfacing as a knoll of duplicated commitment that auditors slash.
